history.sg_progress: The Administration will undertake a study on contingent-owned equipment to support the continuing efforts to strengthen the management of ammunition. The study, which was delayed because of conflicting priorities and the ongoing pandemic, will be carried out by an integrated team of staff from relevant offices in the Department of Peace Operations and the Department of Operational Support. The objective of the study is to conduct a comprehensive review of the status of implementation of recommendations relating to weapons and ammunition management and the United Nations Manual on Ammunition Management; to identify shortcomings that could pose a risk to the safety and security of personnel and property or negatively impact operational readiness and mandate implementation; and to make practical recommendations to strengthen ammunition management in field missions.

history.recommendation_text: In paragraph 209 of its report, the Board recommended that the Administration analyse the direct and indirect costs associated with the disposal of unserviceable and expired ammunition from troop- and/or police-contributing countries and inform Member States accordingly.
history.reference_raw: Recommendations contained in the report of the Board of Auditors for the 12 -month period ended 30 June 2018 ( A/73/5 (Vol. II)
history.sg_progress: Ammunition management is a task for which responsibility is shared across the Organization, including several departments and missions. When the Department of Operational Support was established, in 2019, ammunition management was not a task envisaged for the Department, for which reason it was not resourced with a specialist to carry out that task. The Department identified the need for resources to perform specialized work on ammunition to be included in the Support Account budget proposals for the 2021/22 financial period and then in the 2022/23 financial period. Given the overall financial situation, however, the decision was taken not to request additional resources for that purpose. In addition, the Department explored the possibility of obtaining an expert as gratis personnel, but no nominations were received. Ultimately, the Department conducted its own assessment and analysis, as recommended by the Board, by overstretching its existing resources. It gave a briefing to Member States on the analysis of ammunition costs in a meeting held on 4 December 2024. The Administration considers this recommendation to have been implemented and requests its closure by the Board.
